fullPassage: Forcing a young child to eat foods she or he does not like, or totally restricting access to favorite foods, can have lifelong negative effects on food preferences and health. When attempts to get a child to eat a particular food turn the dinner table into a battleground for control, nobody wins. Foods should be offered in an objective, nonthreatening way so that the child has a fair chance to try the food and make a decision about it. Restricting access to, or prohibiting intake of, children's favorite "junk" foods tends to strengthen their interest in the foods and consumption of those foods when they get a chance. Such prohibitions have the opposite effect of that intended because they make kids want the foods even more.

questions.passage: Foods should be offered in an objective, nonthreatening way so that the child has a fair chance to try the food and make a __________ (decide) about it.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

make a __________ (decide) about it

det.korean: decide(동사) → decision(명사): make a decision = ~에 대한 결정을 내리다. 'make a' 뒤에는 명사가 필요.
det.analysis: make a + 명사 구조 → decision (동사원형 decide의 명사형). 'make a decide'는 불가.
det.tip: make a decision(결정을 내리다) — decide(동사) → decision(명사). 동명사/원형 불가.

overlay.excerptSentences: Foods should be offered in an objective, nonthreatening way so that the child has a fair chance to try the food and make a __________ (decide) about it.

questions.passage: Such prohibitions have the opposite effect of that __________ (intend) because they make kids want the foods even more.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

the opposite effect of that __________ (intend)

det.korean: intend(동사원형) → intended(과거분사): 'that intended'는 'the effect that was intended'에서 관계사절 축약. 수동 의미이므로 과거분사.
det.analysis: that + 과거분사 → intended (관계사절 축약형 수동). '의도된 효과와 반대의 효과를 가짐'.
det.tip: that intended = that was intended(의도된) — 관계사절 축약 + 수동 과거분사.

overlay.excerptSentences: Such prohibitions have the opposite effect of that __________ (intend) because they make kids want the foods even more.

questions.passage: Forcing a young child to eat foods she or he does not like, or totally restricting access to favorite foods, can have lifelong negative effects on food preferences and health. When attempts to get a child to eat a particular food turn the dinner table into a battleground for control, __________. Foods should be offered in an objective, nonthreatening way so that the child has a fair chance to try the food and make a decision about it. Restricting access to, or prohibiting intake of, children's favorite "junk" foods tends to strengthen their interest in the foods and consumption of those foods when they get a chance. Such prohibitions have the opposite effect of that intended because they make kids want the foods even more.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: nobody wins(아무도 이기지 못한다) — 식탁이 통제를 위한 전쟁터가 되면 결국 부모도 아이도 얻는 것이 없다는 글의 논지. 강요와 제한이 모두에게 손해임을 요약.
det.analysis:
❌ ① the child becomes healthier: 식탁 갈등이 건강에 좋다는 의미, 논지와 반대
✅ ② nobody wins: 원문 일치 — 갈등으로 변하면 누구도 이득 없음
❌ ③ parents achieve their goal: 부모가 목표 달성, 글에서는 강요가 역효과라고 함
❌ ④ the food tastes better: 음식 맛, 통제 갈등 맥락과 무관
det.tip: turn the dinner table into a battleground for control, nobody wins — 싸움이 되면 누구도 얻는 것이 없다.

questions.passage: Forcing a young child to eat foods she or he does not like, or totally restricting access to favorite foods, can have lifelong negative effects on food preferences and health. When attempts to get a child to eat a particular food turn the dinner table into a battleground for control, nobody wins. Foods should be offered in an objective, nonthreatening way so that the child has a fair chance to try the food and make a decision about it. Restricting access to, or prohibiting intake of, children's favorite "junk" foods tends to strengthen their interest in the foods and consumption of those foods when they get a chance. Such prohibitions have __________ because they make kids want the foods even more.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: the opposite effect of that intended(의도한 것과 반대의 효과) — 음식 금지가 오히려 그 음식에 대한 욕구를 더 키운다는 역설적 결과. 본문 전체 논지의 핵심.
det.analysis:
❌ ① an immediate improvement in eating habits: 즉각적인 식습관 개선, 글의 역설 논지와 반대
✅ ② the opposite effect of that intended: 원문 일치 — 금지가 의도와 반대 효과를 낳음
❌ ③ a reduction in the child's food interest: 관심 감소, 글에서는 오히려 관심이 강화된다고 함
❌ ④ a stronger bond between parent and child: 부모-자녀 유대 강화, 음식 맥락과 무관
det.tip: Such prohibitions have the opposite effect of that intended — 금지가 의도와 반대 결과를 낳는다는 역설.
